text: At the time of the events in question, Hyde Park was registered with the Moldovan Ministry of Justice as a non-governmental organisation.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: Hyde Park lobbied, among other things, for freedom of expression and the right to free assembly.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: In 2007, Hyde Park's members decided to discontinue registration with the Moldovan Ministry of Justice.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: Hyde Park's members decided to discontinue registration on grounds of alleged pressure and intimidation from the State.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: Hyde Park's members complained of the refusal of the Moldovan Ministry of Justice to register amendments to Hyde Park's articles of association.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: Hyde Park's members complained of the repeated freezing of Hyde Park's bank account.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: Hyde Park's members complained of arbitrary arrest of Hyde Park's members.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: Hyde Park's members complained of attempts to shut down Hyde Park's newspaper.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: Hyde Park's members complained of other interferences by the State in addition to those specifically listed.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: Several of Hyde Park's leaders requested political asylum in western countries.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: It was decided that Hyde Park would continue its activity under the same name but without being registered with the State authorities.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: It was decided that the new unincorporated association would become the former registered organisation's successor.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: After Hyde Park was struck off the Government's list of non-governmental organisations, on 2 June 2008, Hyde Park's activity continued on the basis of new articles of association.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: After 2 June 2008, all of Hyde Park's activities were carried on.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: Hyde Park continued editing its newspaper after being struck off the Government's list of non-governmental organisations.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: Hyde Park continued editing its internet page after being struck off the Government's list of non-governmental organisations.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: Hyde Park continued staging protests and demonstrations after being struck off the Government's list of non-governmental organisations.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: On 23 July 2007, Hyde Park applied to the Municipal Council of Chișinău for authorisation to stage a protest on 30 August 2007.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: The planned protest of 30 August 2007 was to be staged in front of the Ministry of Internal Affairs and the Prosecutor General's Office.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: The planned protest of 30 August 2007 was against alleged acts of harassment of Hyde Park by the Ministry of Internal Affairs and the Prosecutor General's Office.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: On 20 August 2007, the Municipal Council of Chișinău authorised the protest planned for 30 August 2007.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: The Municipal Council of Chișinău authorised the protest to be staged in front of the building of the Ministry of Internal Affairs between 7.30 a.m. and 8.15 a.m. on 30 August 2007.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: The Municipal Council of Chișinău authorised the protest to be staged in front of the Prosecutor General's Office between 8.15 a.m. and 9 a.m. on 30 August 2007.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: The authorisation required the protest to be held at a distance of at least fifty metres from the buildings of the Ministry of Internal Affairs and the Prosecutor General's Office.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: On 30 August 2007, at 7.30 a.m., the applicants started their protest in front of the Ministry of Internal Affairs.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: Immediately after the applicants started their protest on 30 August 2007, a police officer approached them and ordered them to stop the protest.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: The police officer ordered the applicants to stop the protest because the Municipal Council of Chișinău's authorisation of 20 August 2007 had been challenged by the Prosecutor General's Office in court on 29 August 2007.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: The police officer argued that according to the Law on the Prosecutor's Office, the prosecutor's appeal against an administrative act suspended the latter's action until after a court examined it.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: The applicants refused to comply with the police officer's order to stop the protest on 30 August 2007.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: The applicants argued that the Municipal Council of Chișinău's authorisation of 20 August 2007 was valid and that their protest was peaceful.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: The applicants relied on the provisions of the Constitution of Moldova and on the Convention in support of their argument that the protest was lawful.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: Shortly after the applicants refused to comply, a police van arrived at the scene of the protest on 30 August 2007.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: Mr Ghenadie Brega was arrested on 30 August 2007 and taken to a police station where he was questioned.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: Mr Oleg Brega was arrested on 30 August 2007 and taken to a police station where he was questioned.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: Mr Hristea-Stan was arrested on 30 August 2007 and taken to a police station where he was questioned.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: Mr Juraveli was arrested on 30 August 2007 and taken to a police station where he was questioned.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: At approximately 9.30 a.m. on 30 August 2007, Mr Ghenadie Brega, Mr Oleg Brega, Mr Hristea-Stan and Mr Juraveli were released without explanation.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: The applicants could not continue their protest on 30 August 2007 because the time indicated in the Municipal Council of Chișinău's authorisation had lapsed.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: On 30 August 2007, a criminal complaint was lodged against the police officers who carried out the arrests of Mr Ghenadie Brega, Mr Oleg Brega, Mr Hristea-Stan and Mr Juraveli.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: The criminal complaint against the police officers who carried out the arrests on 30 August 2007 was dismissed by the head of the police station of the Centru District on 19 September 2007.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: The head of the police station of the Centru District dismissed the criminal complaint on the ground that the Municipal Council of Chișinău's authorisation of 20 August 2007 contained numerous flaws, including a failure to indicate the exact place of the protest.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: The head of the police station of the Centru District dismissed the criminal complaint on the ground that the Municipal Council of Chișinău's authorisation of 20 August 2007 failed to indicate the number of participants.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: The Prosecutor General's Office's appeal against the Municipal Council of Chișinău's authorisation of 20 August 2007 appears never to have been examined by the courts.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: On 30 August 2007, Mr Juraveli, the vice-president of Hyde Park, applied to the Municipal Council of Chișinău for an authorisation to stage a protest in front of the Ministry of Internal Affairs and the Prosecutor General's Office between 4 and 11 September 2007.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: The planned protest between 4 and 11 September 2007 was against the allegedly abusive suppression of Hyde Park's peaceful protest of 30 August 2007.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: In the application for authorisation for the protest between 4 and 11 September 2007, Mr Juraveli indicated that ten persons were to participate in the demonstration.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: In the application for authorisation for the protest between 4 and 11 September 2007, Mr Juraveli gave his own name as one of those responsible for the conduct of the demonstration.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: In the application for authorisation for the protest between 4 and 11 September 2007, Mr Juraveli gave the name of Mr Oleg Brega as one of those responsible for the conduct of the demonstration.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: In the application for authorisation for the protest between 4 and 11 September 2007, Mr Juraveli gave the name of Mr Hristea-Stan as one of those responsible for the conduct of the demonstration.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: The Municipal Council of Chișinău did not adopt a decision in respect of Mr Juraveli's application of 30 August 2007 before the first date of the planned demonstration, 4 September 2007.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: At 9 a.m. on 4 September 2007, the applicants started their protest in front of the Ministry of Internal Affairs.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: At 9.25 a.m. on 4 September 2007, Mr Ghenadie Brega was arrested on the ground that the demonstration had not been authorised.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: At 9.25 a.m. on 4 September 2007, Mr Oleg Brega was arrested on the ground that the demonstration had not been authorised.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: At 9.25 a.m. on 4 September 2007, a Hyde Park member who is not an applicant in the present case was arrested on the ground that the demonstration had not been authorised.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: Mr Ghenadie Brega, Mr Oleg Brega and the non-applicant Hyde Park member were taken to a police station on 4 September 2007 where they were body searched.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: Mr Ghenadie Brega, Mr Oleg Brega and the non-applicant Hyde Park member were kept at the police station for approximately five hours on 4 September 2007.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: According to the applicants, the police examined and made copies of the detained persons' documents, including personal letters, on 4 September 2007.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: Two of the persons detained on 4 September 2007 were placed in cages and later in cells at the police station.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: The persons detained on 4 September 2007 were later taken to the Centru District Court.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: Since the hearing at the Centru District Court was adjourned, the persons detained on 4 September 2007 were released at 3 p.m. that day.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: On 21 September 2007, the Centru District Court examined the charges against the applicants arising from the demonstration of 4 September 2007.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: The applicants argued before the Centru District Court that since the Municipal Council of Chișinău had failed to examine their application for authorisation before the date of the demonstration, they had the right to hold the demonstration in accordance with section 12(5) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: The applicants submitted to the Centru District Court that they had been told by a representative of the local authorities that the Municipal Council of Chișinău did not have time to deal with their request and that they could hold their protest as planned.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: The Centru District Court dismissed the applicants' submissions regarding the demonstration of 4 September 2007.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: The Centru District Court found that the applicants had breached section 11(1) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 by failing to submit the application within fifteen days in advance of the planned assembly.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: According to the Centru District Court, the protest should have been held on 14 September 2007 at the earliest.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: The Centru District Court found Mr Ghenadie Brega guilty of organising an unauthorised demonstration and fined him 800 Moldovan lei (approximately 48 euros).
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: The Centru District Court found Mr Oleg Brega guilty of organising an unauthorised demonstration and fined him 800 Moldovan lei (approximately 48 euros).
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: Another Hyde Park member who is not an applicant in the present case was fined 200 Moldovan lei by the Centru District Court in connection with the demonstration of 4 September 2007.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: The applicants appealed against the Centru District Court's judgment regarding the demonstration of 4 September 2007.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: The applicants' appeal was dismissed by the Chișinău Court of Appeal on the same grounds on 23 October 2007.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: On 7 September 2007, the Municipal Council of Chișinău examined Mr Juraveli's application of 30 August 2007 for authorisation to stage a protest.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: On 7 September 2007, the Municipal Council of Chișinău issued an authorisation to Mr Juraveli to organise and stage a protest in front of the buildings of the Ministry of Internal Affairs and the Prosecutor General's Office between 8 and 11 September 2007.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: In the morning of 10 September 2007, several members of Hyde Park started to protest in front of the buildings of the Ministry of Internal Affairs and the Prosecutor General's Office.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: Several minutes after the Hyde Park members began protesting on 10 September 2007, the police arrived and arrested Mr Juraveli on the ground that the authorisation did not contain the names of all the persons involved in the protest.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: Several minutes after the Hyde Park members began protesting on 10 September 2007, the police arrived and arrested Mr Oleg Brega on the ground that the authorisation did not contain the names of all the persons involved in the protest.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: Several minutes after the Hyde Park members began protesting on 10 September 2007, the police arrived and arrested Mr Hristea-Stan on the ground that the authorisation did not contain the names of all the persons involved in the protest.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: The Government maintained that Mr Juraveli, Mr Oleg Brega and Mr Hristea-Stan had been detained on 10 September 2007 for breach of the peace and for having shouted insults about the Minister for Internal Affairs.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: At the police station on 10 September 2007, Mr Juraveli, Mr Oleg Brega and Mr Hristea-Stan were questioned and searched.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: Mr Juraveli, Mr Oleg Brega and Mr Hristea-Stan were released after five hours of detention on 10 September 2007.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: The applicants maintained that, while detained on 10 September 2007, they were not allowed to make any telephone calls or to contact a lawyer.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: The police filed administrative proceedings against Mr Juraveli, Mr Oleg Brega and Mr Hristea-Stan following their arrest on 10 September 2007.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: On 21 September 2007, the Centru District Court decided to discontinue the administrative proceedings filed against Mr Juraveli, Mr Oleg Brega and Mr Hristea-Stan in connection with the events of 10 September 2007.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: On 5 September 2007, Mr Oleg Brega wrote to the Prosecutor General making a criminal complaint in respect of the actions of the police at the demonstration of 30 August 2007.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: On 5 September 2007, Mr Oleg Brega wrote to the Prosecutor General making a criminal complaint in respect of the actions of the police at the demonstration of 4 September 2007.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: A further letter to the Prosecutor General regarding the criminal complaint about police actions at the demonstrations of 30 August and 4 September 2007 was sent on 10 January 2008.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASES

text: The applicants maintain that they did not receive an official response to either letter sent to the Prosecutor General on 5 September 2007 and 10 January 2008.

text: Article 32(1) of the Constitution of the Republic of Moldova guarantees each citizen freedom of thought, of opinion, and freedom of expression in public through words, images or through other available means.
Article 32(2) of the Constitution of the Republic of Moldova provides that freedom of expression shall not harm the honour or dignity of others or the right of others to have their own opinion.

Article 32(3) of the Constitution of the Republic of Moldova provides that the law prohibits and punishes the contestation and defamation of the State and the nation, calls to war and aggression, national, racial or religious hatred, incitement to discrimination, territorial separatism, or public violence, as well as other expression which endangers the constitutional order.

Article 40 of the Constitution of the Republic of Moldova provides that all meetings, demonstrations, rallies, processions or any other assemblies are free, and they may be organised and take place only peacefully and without the use of weapons.

Section 6(1) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that assemblies shall be conducted peacefully, without any sort of weapons, and shall ensure the protection of participants and the environment, without impeding the normal use of public highways, road traffic and the operation of economic undertakings and without degenerating into acts of violence capable of endangering the public order and the physical integrity and life of persons or their property.

Section 7 of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that assemblies shall be suspended in circumstances including denial and defamation of the State and of the people, incitement to war or aggression, incitement to hatred on ethnic, racial or religious grounds, incitement to discrimination, territorial separatism or public violence, and acts that undermine the constitutional order.

Section 8(1) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that assemblies may be conducted in squares, streets, parks and other public places in cities, towns and villages, and also in public buildings.

Section 8(2) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that it shall be forbidden to conduct an assembly in the buildings of the public authorities, the local authorities, prosecutors' offices, the courts or companies with armed security.

Section 8(3)(a) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that it shall be forbidden to conduct assemblies within fifty metres of the parliament building, the residence of the President of Moldova, the seat of the government, the Constitutional Court and the Supreme Court of Justice.

Section 8(3)(b) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that it shall be forbidden to conduct assemblies within twenty-five metres of the buildings of the central administrative authority, the local public authorities, courts, prosecutors' offices, police stations, prisons and social rehabilitation institutions, military installations, railway stations, airports, hospitals, companies which use dangerous equipment and machines, and diplomatic institutions.
Section 8(4) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that free access to the premises of the institutions listed in section 8(3) shall be guaranteed.
Section 8(5) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that the local public authorities may, if the organisers agree, establish places or buildings for permanent assemblies.
Section 11(1) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that not later than fifteen days prior to the date of the assembly, the organiser shall submit a notification to the Municipal Council.

Section 11(2) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that the prior notification shall indicate the name of the organiser and the aim of the assembly, the date, starting time and finishing time, the location and access and return routes, the manner in which the assembly is to take place, the approximate number of participants, the persons responsible for the sound conduct of the assembly, and the services the organiser asks the Municipal Council to provide.

Section 11(3) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that if the situation so requires, the Municipal Council may alter certain aspects of the prior notification with the agreement of the organiser of the assembly.

Section 12(1) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that the prior notification shall be examined by the local government of the town or village at the latest five days before the date of the assembly.

Section 12(2) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that when the prior notification is considered at an ordinary or extraordinary meeting of the Municipal Council, the discussion shall deal with the form, timetable, location and other conditions for the conduct of the assembly and the decision taken shall take account of the specific situation.

Section 12(6) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that the local authorities can reject an application to hold an assembly only if, after having consulted the police, it has obtained convincing evidence that the provisions of sections 6 and 7 of the Assemblies Act will be breached with serious consequences for society.

Section 14(1) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that a decision rejecting the application for holding an assembly shall be reasoned and presented in writing, and shall contain reasons for refusing to issue the authorisation.
Section 15(1) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that the organiser of the assembly can challenge the refusal in the administrative courts.

Section 19 of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that participants at the assembly are required to respect the Act and other laws referred to therein, to respect the instructions of the organiser of the assembly and decisions of the municipality or police, and to leave the assembly if asked by the organiser, the municipality or the police.

Article 166(1) of the Criminal Code of Moldova provides that illegal deprivation of liberty, if it is not a kidnapping, shall be punishable with community work of 120-240 hours or imprisonment of up to 2 years.

Article 166(2) of the Criminal Code of Moldova provides that illegal deprivation of liberty committed against two or more persons or by two or more persons shall be punishable with imprisonment of 3 to 8 years.

Article 184(1) of the Criminal Code of Moldova provides that violation of the right to freedom of assembly by way of illegal hindering of a demonstration, rally or action of protest or hindering of persons from taking part in them, when committed by an official, by two or more persons, or accompanied by acts of violence which are not dangerous to life or health, shall be punishable with a fine of four to eight thousand Moldovan lei or with community work of 180-240 hours, or with imprisonment of up to two years.

Article 174 § 1(2) of the Code of Administrative Offences, in force at the material time, provided that the organisation and holding of an assembly without prior notification to the Municipal Council or without authorisation from the Council, or in breach of the conditions concerning the conduct of meetings indicated in the authorisation, shall be punishable by a fine on the organisers (leaders) of the assembly in an amount equal to between 500 and 1,000 Moldovan lei.

Article 174 § 1(4) of the Code of Administrative Offences, in force at the material time, provided that active participation in an assembly referred to in paragraph 2 of Article 174 § 1 shall be punishable by a fine in an amount between 200 and 300 Moldovan lei.

Article 174 § 5 of the Code of Administrative Offences, in force at the material time, provided that resisting a police officer in the exercise of his or her duties of ensuring public order and the fight against crime shall be punishable by a fine up to 300 Moldovan lei or detention of up to thirty days.

Article 174 § 6 of the Code of Administrative Offences, in force at the material time, provided that insulting police officers in the exercise of their duties shall be punishable by a fine of up to 200 Moldovan lei or imprisonment of up to fifteen days.
Article 14 of the Civil Code of Moldova provides that any person whose rights have been infringed may request full compensation in respect of the damage thus caused.

The relevant provisions of Law no. 1545 (1998) on compensation for damage caused by the illegal acts of the criminal investigation organs, prosecution and courts have been set out in the Court's judgment in Sarban v. Moldova, no. 3456/05, § 54, 4 October 2005.

In the case of Belicevecen v. the Ministry of Finance (no. 2ra-1171/07, 4 July 2007), the Supreme Court of Justice of Moldova found that a person could claim damages on the basis of Law no. 1545 (1998) only if he or she had been fully acquitted of all the charges against him or her.

In the case of Belicevecen v. the Ministry of Finance (no. 2ra-1171/07, 4 July 2007), since Mr Belicevecen had been found guilty in respect of one of the charges brought against him, the Supreme Court of Justice of Moldova found he could not claim any damages under Law no. 1545 (1998).
